title: Checkpoint: Castles and Palaces
objective: After this level you can compare buildings made to defend with buildings made to impress.
summary: Guns ended the castle age in 1494. Castles had already grown comfortable, and English barons moved to country houses. Defend, impress, or both: every building here chose.

cards.headline: Chapter 4 finale: in 1494, guns took castle after castle.
cards.body: French troops marched through Italy, and their guns reduced castle after castle with astonishing speed. With firearms, the age of the medieval castle ended and modern military fortification began. A building made to defend had met an attack it could not answer.

cards.headline: From fortress to show-off
cards.body: Castles were already changing. As households grew and lords wanted privacy, they built larger ranges of rooms. At Bodiam, buildings were set around a central courtyard with a tower at each corner, so their inner faces could risk large windows. Then under the strong central rule of the Tudors, English barons stopped building castles and moved into country houses. Defense was giving way to comfort and display.

mascot.line: Big windows are a sign of confidence. Nobody plans on arrows through the living room.

cards.headline: Castles and Palaces: defend, impress, or both

items.label: Built to defend
points: The Great Wall, built by many governments (Level 32)

items.label: Built to impress
points: Versailles, with nobles under the king's eye (Level 37)

items.label: Both at once
points: The Forbidden City, behind a wall and moat (Level 34)
The Alhambra: plain fortress outside, ornate inside (Level 35)

cards.headline: Chapter 4 complete
learned: Castles were homes built to be attacked; guns ended them
Late castles traded defense for rooms and windows
Palaces house rulers and government, and impress
Some buildings did both: the Forbidden City, the Alhambra

questions.prompt: Castles and Palaces checkpoint: what happened when French troops marched through Italy in 1494?

options.label: Their miners burned the props under every keep
options.rationale: Mining was older; 1494 was about guns.

options.label: Their guns took castle after castle, fast
They built new round towers all across Italy
options.rationale: They were attacking castles, not building them.

options.label: They moved the royal court into Versailles
options.rationale: Versailles became the royal home in 1682.

questions.explanation: Their guns took castle after castle quickly, and the age of the medieval castle ended.

questions.prompt: Castles and Palaces checkpoint: why could a late castle like Bodiam risk large windows?

options.label: Its glass was strong enough to stop arrows
options.rationale: Nothing like that; it was the layout.

options.label: Its outer walls were thicker than any keep
options.rationale: The windows were about the plan, not wall thickness.

options.label: It was built after guns had ended all sieges
options.rationale: It dates from before the 1494 campaign.

options.label: Its rooms faced an inner courtyard

questions.explanation: At Bodiam, buildings were set around a central courtyard with a tower at each corner, so their inner faces could risk large windows.

options.label: The Taj Mahal

questions.prompt: Castles and Palaces recap: which part of a square tower did miners find easiest to undermine?

options.label: The flat roof
options.rationale: Miners dug underneath, not on top.

options.label: The arrow loops
Its corners
The wooden door
options.rationale: Mining attacked the foundations of a corner.

questions.explanation: Miners tunnelled under a corner, filled the hole with wood and fired it; round towers had no corners to attack.

questions.prompt: Castles and Palaces recap: what does NASA say about seeing the Great Wall from space?

options.label: It's the one human-made thing visible from the Moon
It shows up clearly at night from the space station
Hard or impossible to see from orbit without lenses
Easy to see from orbit, but only after snowfall

questions.explanation: NASA says the wall isn't visible from the Moon and is difficult or impossible to see from Earth orbit without high-powered lenses.
